result:
`is_supported_version` in `mitmproxy/net/tls.py` no longer crashes when an OpenSSL build rejects a protocol version. I didn't run any tests, and I didn't add one.

Setting the min/max protocol version on the probe context is now wrapped in `try/except SSL.Error`. If either call raises, the function returns `False`, so that version is treated as unsupported. The existing handling of the connection probe is unchanged.

I also added a bullet for this fix to `CHANGELOG.md` under "Unreleased".

diff --git a/CHANGELOG.md b/CHANGELOG.md
index 250d4bdea..07a54bdc6 100644
--- a/CHANGELOG.md
+++ b/CHANGELOG.md
@@ -7,6 +7,8 @@
 
 ## Unreleased: mitmproxy next
 
+- Fix a crash when probing supported TLS versions on OpenSSL builds that reject
+  setting the minimum/maximum protocol version.
 - mitmweb: Reduce FlowTable Redux subscriptions from O(rows) to O(1).
   ([#8104](https://github.com/mitmproxy/mitmproxy/pull/8104), @ariel42)
 - mitmweb: Fix editors not allowing content to be cleared to an empty string
diff --git a/mitmproxy/net/tls.py b/mitmproxy/net/tls.py
index 14c0553ca..d914857de 100644
--- a/mitmproxy/net/tls.py
+++ b/mitmproxy/net/tls.py
@@ -77,8 +77,12 @@ def is_supported_version(version: Version):
     # Without SECLEVEL, recent OpenSSL versions forbid old TLS versions.
     # https://github.com/pyca/cryptography/issues/9523
     client_ctx.set_cipher_list(b"@SECLEVEL=0:ALL")
-    client_ctx.set_min_proto_version(version.value)
-    client_ctx.set_max_proto_version(version.value)
+    try:
+        client_ctx.set_min_proto_version(version.value)
+        client_ctx.set_max_proto_version(version.value)
+    except SSL.Error:
+        # Some OpenSSL builds reject versions they were compiled without.
+        return False
     client_conn = SSL.Connection(client_ctx)
     client_conn.set_connect_state()
